localBiteReport: Note: The most recent Destin-area inshore blog reports are about 3 weeks old — Half Hitch's latest Destin report is dated 9-28-26, and no October Destin edition has posted yet. That said, here's what the current picture looks like: Hurricane Isaias made landfall at Destin on October 9, causing significant damage to the marina on Choctawhatchee Bay, and post-storm water conditions have been variable. Despite that, guides working the bay report that redfish and trout activity in the bayous and on the flats has been heating up as fall sets in, with slot reds being picked up around docks and deeper drop-offs, and trout remaining active — particularly in low-light hours. Flounder are considered to be in one of their best months of the year for this area during October, concentrating along grass flat edges and sandy transitions as water cools. Sheepshead are expected to begin stacking on bridge pilings and structure in the coming weeks as temperatures continue to drop. Water temp on the bay is 78°F.
